title: DSM App access
admin_required: This App requires a DSM administrator.
group_required: Your DSM account is not in a group allowed to use this App. Contact your DSM administrator.
sign_in_required: Sign in to DSM on this address first, then try again.
verification_failed: DSM could not verify your sign-in. Try again in a moment.
direct_notice: DSM-managed HTTPS is unavailable for this App. The direct connection may show a certificate warning or use unencrypted HTTP.
app_privilege_denied: Your DSM account is not allowed to use this App. Contact your DSM administrator.
share_steps: Ask an administrator to open Control Panel > Shared Folder > {folder} > Edit > Permissions > System internal user > {account} > {access}
share_ready: Access is ready. Start this App in Package Center
share_next_start: After granting access, start this App again in Package Center
share_unavailable: Shared Folder status is unavailable. Check the folder selection and start this App again in Package Center
starting: The App is starting or temporarily busy. This page refreshes automatically.
external_dsm_missing: Open DSM from your local network and configure the DSM address in this App’s external access settings
external_signin: Sign in to DSM, then reload this page
external_denied: A verified DSM administrator session and SynoToken are required
external_private_hint: Open Connect to view private addresses
external_format: Public address: https://DNS-name, with no path or port other than 443; leave blank to clear
external_format_single: Address: https://DNS-name, with no path; a port is allowed, for example https://nas.example.ts.net:28443 for a tailnet address on the App port; leave blank to clear
external_confirm: I confirm that changing the address may affect passkeys and sign-in
external_restart: Restart the App for its container environment to use the new address
external_protected: According to the App settings, web access requires DSM sign-in
external_upstream: This App uses its own sign-in; some pages may be public
external_optional: An administrator may have opened these paths:
external_warning: The DSM sign-in page is also public when using a public address; enable two-step verification because tunnel connections come from 127.0.0.1 and DSM auto-block may not work
external_confirm_single: I confirm that afterwards only the address above can be used to sign in
external_tailnet: This is a Tailscale address: only devices on your tailnet can reach it, unless it is shared with Funnel
menu_title: This App cannot be opened from this address
menu_unavailable: This App cannot be opened from the DSM address you are using. Ask your administrator
menu_not_enabled: You are using DSM through {provider}, but this App has no {provider} address yet
menu_not_enabled_hint: Turn it on in the App URLs page of NAS Remote Connect to open it from here
menu_paused: This App's {provider} address is paused in NAS Remote Connect
menu_unreachable_title: This App cannot be reached right now
menu_unreachable: The App may be stopped or upgrading, or its address may be paused
menu_quickconnect_title: Apps cannot be opened through QuickConnect
menu_quickconnect: QuickConnect reaches DSM only, not Apps. Use a private network or public address
menu_single_local: This App can sign in at one address only, and it has no address for this connection. Set its address in the App's external access settings
menu_single_unreachable: This App can sign in at one address only, and this device cannot reach it now
menu_single_tailnet: A Tailscale address can be reached only from devices on the tailnet
menu_connect: Set up this App in Connect
menu_connect_missing: Install NAS Remote Connect from Package Center to give this App an address for this connection
menu_settings: Open the App's external access settings
